sessionTitle: Protein preparation, gels, and Western blot

representative.title: Cell lysis and extraction of total protein from Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 v1
representative.operation: Total protein extraction with separable soluble and insoluble fractions
representative.methodVariant: Total protein extraction; soluble and insoluble fractions may be separated
representative.selectionNote: Selected as the strongest direct extraction record because its title, abstract, DOI, author, dates, organism, and downstream protein-use context are explicit. This is a cyanobacterial variant, so mammalian, plant, tissue, membrane, and organelle extraction chemistries remain separate child variants rather than being silently mixed.

screened.title: Whole cell protein extraction and Western blotting v1
screened.reason: Relevant whole-cell extraction and blotting workflow, but it couples extraction to Western blotting and is less cleanly scoped to extraction alone.

screened.title: Cell lysis for preparation of protein extracts for quantitative proteomics - Kryptoperidinium foliaceum, Nitzschia laevis and Symbiodinium sp. v1
screened.reason: Protein extraction is in scope, but the record is a multi-organism quantitative-proteomics preparation variant rather than a general soluble lysate protocol.

screened.title: Cell lysis and gel electrophoresis for protein analysis of HeLa cells v1
screened.reason: Relevant lysis context, but the record combines extraction with gel electrophoresis and is specifically tied to HeLa cells.

coverageGaps: Soluble extraction chemistry varies materially by organism, tissue, membrane association, and organelle; a universal extraction representative would be misleading.
The selected record does not expose a platform facet or detailed inhibitor panel in the metadata-only view.
nextSearchSuggestions: Add mammalian cultured-cell RIPA or detergent-compatible soluble lysate child category.
Add plant/tissue and membrane-protein extraction child categories if those materials are in scope.

representative.title: BCA Assay for protein quantification v1
representative.operation: Protein concentration determination using a BCA assay and protein standard curve
representative.specimen: Protein sample; exact specimen not specified in record metadata
representative.platform: BCA colorimetric assay; kit/platform not specified in record metadata
representative.methodVariant: BCA assay; standard protein identity and sample compatibility should be confirmed from the full record before execution
representative.selectionNote: Selected because it is directly titled for protein quantification, has a stable DOI-backed protocols.io record, and is corroborated by Thermo Fisher's BCA user guide and the UC Berkeley QB3 BCA teaching protocol as the relevant assay family. BSA/HSA standard choice and detergent/reducing-agent compatibility are not inferred beyond the available metadata.

screened.title: Bradford Protein Assay v1
screened.reason: In-scope protein concentration assay, but Bradford chemistry is a distinct assay variant from the selected BCA representative.

screened.title: Pierce BCA Protein Assay Protocol v1
screened.reason: Direct BCA alternative with a named commercial kit; retained as a screened record because the selected title is more generic and cleaner for the category label.

screened.title: Total crude protein in plankton:Pierce BCA protein assay (including the enhanced assay for low biomass) v2
screened.reason: BCA chemistry is relevant, but the workflow is specifically optimized for plankton and low biomass.

coverageGaps: BCA, Bradford, detergent-compatible, reducing-agent-compatible, low-biomass, and microplate/cuvette variants have different interference and calibration facets.
The selected record metadata does not identify the standard protein or readout platform; those fields require checking the full protocol record.
nextSearchSuggestions: Split BCA and Bradford into child categories if assay chemistry is to be operationally reproducible.
Add low-biomass and detergent/reducing-agent compatibility facets to the assay schema.

representative.title: SDS-PAGE Gel Electrophoresis v1
representative.assay: Sodium dodecyl sulfate polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis
representative.specimen: Protein sample; exact specimen not specified in record metadata
representative.platform: Polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis; apparatus not specified in record metadata
representative.methodVariant: Denaturing SDS-PAGE; record notes resolution limits for proteins below approximately 10 kDa and possible gradient/Tricine alternatives
representative.selectionNote: Selected because the record is explicitly titled for SDS-PAGE gel electrophoresis, identifies the denaturing separation context, and notes the small-protein resolution boundary and gradient/Tricine alternatives. Gel percentage, reducing-agent condition, and sample type are not assumed from the title.

screened.title: Polyacrylamide Gel Electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) v1
screened.reason: Directly in-scope SDS-PAGE record, retained as an alternative because the selected record has a more explicit assay title and small-protein variant note.

screened.title: SDS-PAGE gel electrophoresis v4
screened.reason: Versioned SDS-PAGE alternative, but the available metadata does not establish a stronger match to the requested generic category than the selected representative.

screened.title: SDS and Clear Native Gel Electrophoresis v1
screened.reason: Combines denaturing SDS and clear-native electrophoresis, so it is broader than the requested SDS-PAGE-only category.

coverageGaps: Gel percentage, gradient versus fixed-percentage gel, reducing versus non-reducing sample preparation, and apparatus vary by target size and sample type.
The record metadata supports the denaturing and small-protein-resolution facets but not a complete gel percentage or reducing-condition facet.
nextSearchSuggestions: Split fixed-percentage, gradient, Tricine, and native/clear-native gel workflows into child variants.
Add explicit gel percentage, reducing-agent, sample type, and electrophoresis platform fields.

representative.title: Western Blot (Tank-Blot) v1
representative.operation: Electrotransfer of SDS-PAGE proteins to a membrane for antibody-based detection
representative.specimen: SDS-PAGE gel protein sample; exact biological specimen not specified in record metadata
representative.platform: Tank-blot electrotransfer; membrane described as PVDF in record metadata
representative.methodVariant: Tank transfer with PVDF membrane followed by antibody staining; transfer buffer and electrical conditions are visible in the source abstract
representative.selectionNote: Selected because it is a dedicated tank-blot record with stable DOI, explicit author/date metadata, and direct metadata describing electrotransfer and PVDF membrane handling. It is a transfer and antibody-staining variant; detection chemistry and antibody targets remain assay-specific facets.

screened.title: Western Blot (tank-blot) + Antibody staining v1
screened.reason: Directly in-scope tank-blot and antibody-staining record, retained as an alternative because the selected record is the cleaner dedicated transfer representative.

screened.title: Western blot protocol v1
screened.reason: Generic Western blot protocol with stable DOI, but its available metadata is less specific about transfer system than the selected tank-blot record.

screened.title: 12% SDS-PAGE Western Blot v1
screened.reason: Combines gel composition and immunoblotting, so it is not a clean Western-blot-only record for this packet.

coverageGaps: Tank transfer and semi-dry transfer are distinct platform variants; membrane choice, transfer buffer, antibody host/conjugate, and chemiluminescent versus fluorescent detection are not interchangeable.
The selected record does not identify target protein, antibody clone, blocking reagent, or detection chemistry in the metadata fields.
nextSearchSuggestions: Split tank-blot and semi-dry transfer into child categories.
Add membrane, blocking chemistry, antibody/detection chemistry, and imaging platform facets.
